notes.title: Sector Unknown - Latest Devlogs Part II
notes.content:
Sector Unknown - Latest Devlogs
Here are some devlogs from my latest sci-fi cRPG that I've been working on. Hope you enjoy! If you like what you see, please feel free to wishlist and follow:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2734270/Sector_Unknown/

[h2]Devlog: The Planets of Sector Unknown[/h2]
A few weeks back, I wrapped up the last of the five story planets for Sector Unknown. There’s still the “point of no return” planet—the climactic final world—to finish, but every planet leading up to it is now fully fleshed out with quests, writing, and design.

Now seems like a good time to share a bit of insight into each of these worlds. Keep in mind, these are just the core story planets—there are also numerous side-mission stations, derelict ships, and other locations scattered throughout the game….

[b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2734270/announcements/detail/539972271823912998]Read More![/url][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915433/258cedcc13d6426ce622c4a8c7844236702a43e7.png[/img]

[h2]Devlog: The Setting[/h2]
As humanity expanded into the cosmos, the narrative of "Sector Unknown" unfolded in a clandestine sector comprising three primary star systems—Xiphos (XPH-6430), Svion (SVN-8912), and Fivo (FIV-6789)—along with several minor ones. These systems were home to the planets Maku, Nabi, Sjo, Eremtera, and Helfyr (more devlogs to come on each of these planets).

For decades, Star Frontier, a colossal trading entity reminiscent of the historical East India Company, attempted to ruthlessly exploit these planets. Operating with impunity due to the sector's erasure from all official star maps, Star Frontier unrelentingly expanded into the sector, unhindered by governmental oversight…

[b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2734270/announcements/detail/518573831795769384]Read More![/url][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44915433/c3002d6391b70cb8a2620a5031c73ca5ebbcd466.png[/img]

[h2]Devlog: Skills, Attributes, and Combat Stats[/h2]

In Sector Unknown, your character and companions will have their own skills and attributes. 

Attributes are commonly used to determine your combat skills, but can occasionally be used to outside of combat as well. Combat stats are derived from your attributes and determine your success in combat. And finally skills are used primarily outside of combat in dialogue, through world interactions, and more. The only skills that can be used in combat is Piloting, which determines your skill in space encounters, and Luck which provide re-rolls on failed critical hits and evasions…

[b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2734270/announcements/detail/4282447070494670109]Read More![/url][/b]

notes.title: Age of Gladiators Reforged - Coming Soon!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11921345/5fa6f42bf2d6a194a640c82681f205d468688f69.png[/img]

It's been a busy Summer.

Along with [i][b]Deadwater Saloon[/b][/i], I would also like to announce [i][b]Age of Gladiators Reforged[/b][/i], a remake of the original 2016 game in the Unity Engine.

The store page can be seen here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2103620/Age_of_Gladiators_Reforged/

As some of you might know, I created the 2016 game in an engine I (barely) cobbled together from several books. It didn't work in most resolutions and UI/quality-of-life changes were near impossible to implement - so I decided to recreate it in Unity from scratch.

The UI has been updated to something made in 2022 (featuring more icons and less text as well as better-looking windows that conform to the overall palette) and many new quality of life additions have been added (daily alert icons across the top for example).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11921345/0e02fdc71435a1a15a26dbc647133c02565cd717.png[/img]

As well, numerous other gameplay and aesthetic changes have been made:

[list]
[*]Combat Mitigation now fed by agility and reflexes as well, making these attributes more useful.
[*]Improved alerts system
[*]Revised Gladiator Expertise system
[*]Revised Player Perks system
[*]Age incline and decline more drastic
[*]Added Killer Instinct and Work Ethic to gladiator personalities
[*]Drastically improved tooltips
[*]Works on most resolutions
[*]Staff, Lender, Other portraits added throughout the UI - now you can put a face to a name
[*]Weapons and Armor now have Stamina costs (making stamina much more important now)
[*]Dodging and Blocking now use Stamina (again, making stamina much more important now)
[*]Greed also affects daily spending of gladiator
[*]Gladiator portraits added to all UI
[*]Stable now contributes to fatigue recovery time
[*]Stable now has countdown for improvements
[*]Custom mouse cursor instead of system one
[*]Added a fight log so players can recap exactly what happened during battle
[*]Scrollbars instead of burdensome next/previous buttons
[*]Animals now have names
[*]More Player Portraits
[*]Fight Setup screens made more efficiently - a fight can now be started with two clicks instead of the many clicks previously
[*]Improved music player
[*]Icons instead of just text
[/list]

These are just some of the changes - there are plenty more I am not thinking of here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11921345/eba73b389169b5fa9d8de8f5c12d04ac684b21dd.png[/img]

Will keep everyone posted. 

[h3]And of course, previous owners of Age of Gladiators will enjoy a discount if they choose to purchase the remastered version.

So please [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2103620/Age_of_Gladiators_Reforged/]wishlist[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2103620/Age_of_Gladiators_Reforged/]follow[/url] Age of Gladiators Reforged today. [/h3]

Thanks!

notes.title: Wasteland Religion - August 13, 2021
notes.content:
Like everything else in the wasteland, the religions there also suck. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/37448f6c26fee1047573c216172d673c1d53af81.png[/img]

[h1]Never go into a major battle without first considering a sacrifice...[/h1]

Your raiders are an unruly and superstitious lot, perhaps offering some water or meat might appease the gods enough to inspire your army to fight a bit better. Sacrifice a bit of beer (sacrilege!) and they might take the offering even more seriously.

However, the option also exists to sacrifice captive workers or even...one of your own raiders, in order to further boost your followers fervor on the battlefield, successfully awakening their blood lust and violent nature. These sacrifices offer significant combat boosts that can make the difference in capturing that settlement you have your eye on. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/ce7755a5cf87feaaa769304ea4f7d9344bfa999f.png[/img]

As well, after battle, you will have a chance to loot either scripture pages which will amplify the duration of bonuses received after a sacrifice, or holy relics which will provide permanent boosts and modifiers to out-of-combat stats. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/1843d7f99ff79bef1fb29baf900eb7f4ccc02862.png[/img]

Hope you enjoy this update!

And remember: in the wasteland, do unto others before they do unto you.

notes.title: Devlog #16 - Combat Classes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/39ea8e8a3edcc85599d7038d05dc0dac9600bf19.png[/img]

In Raiders, there are three classes:
[list]
[*] [b]Masochist[/b]
[*] [b]Hellion[/b]
[*] [b]Brutician[/b]
[/list]
These follow similar playstyles as existing games, with Hellions causing damage in a variety of ways, Masochists being more sturdy, and Bruticians having an array of support abilities.
Each class has four tiers of Perks that can be unlocked after spending points when leveling up. Each Perk is either passive or activated during combat.

Here are the perks for each.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/94b1493d9b9999302ae5f8ec34f84cf08d12f282.png[/img]

[h1][b]Hellion[/b][/h1]
[i]“I enjoy hurting others. Havoc will be wrought and blood shall be spilled when I wade into battle.”[/i]
[list]
[*] [b]Risky Business:[/b] (+5%) Critical %, (-1) Armor Points For Duration Of Combat
[*] [b]Digging Death: [/b](+2) Damage
[*] [b]Dickhead:[/b] (+2) Critical Damage For Every Dead Team Member
[*] [b]Opposites Attract:[/b] (+1) Damage For Each Opponent With Over (40) Hit Points
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]Up The Gut:[/b] Standard Attack Allowing Targeting Of Second Row, Bypass Attack Roll
[*] [b]Blood Scent:[/b] (+5) Damage On Bleeding Target
[*] [b]Agile Mover: [/b](+2) Critical Damage If Wearing Light Or Medium Armor
[*] [b]I Spit At Thee:[/b] (+25%) Hit % If Below (5) Hitpoints.
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]Hold My Beer:[/b] Deal (+15) Damage During Attack, Reduce Stamina To (0), Bypass Attack Roll
[*] [b]Master Shredder:[/b] (+5) Critical Damage Vs All Light and Medium Armored Targets
[*] [b]Wall Banger:[/b] (+5) Critical Damage Vs All Heavy and Full Armored Targets
[*] [b]Keen To Kill:[/b] (+50) Initiative
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]See You In Hell: [/b]Deal (+20) Damage During Attack, Reduce Hitpoint To (10), Bypass Attack Roll
[*] [b]Do Unto Others:[/b] (+10) Hit % If Enemy Has Over (25%) Critical %
[*] [b]Ganker:[/b] (+5) Critical Damage For Each Team Kill
[*] [b]Born To Kill:[/b] (+5) Damage If Initiative Over 120
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/82995ae6fd3949ca9b9a4c79cef6dd9df57538b9.png[/img]

[h1][b]Masochist[/b][/h1]
[i]“I don't mind a bit of pain. You could try and take me down, but you might hurt yourself…”[/i]
[list]
[*] [b]Idiot's Bellow:[/b] (+5) Hitpoints, (-1) Armor For Duration Of Combat
[*] [b]Leather Skin:[/b] (+5) Hitpoints   
[*] [b]Agent Of Shield:[/b] (+5) Hitpoints If Equipped With Shield
[*] [b]Opposites Attract: [/b](+1) Hitpoint For Each Opponent With Over (30) Hit Damage
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]Shake It Off:[/b] Removes All Negative Effects
[*] [b]Head Banger: [/b](+10) Hitpoints If Equipped With Helmet
[*] [b]Colossus:[/b] (+10) Hitpoints If Equipped With Armor
[*] [b]Wild Thing: [/b](+1) Armor Points if Bleeding
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]Hunker Down:[/b] (+1) Armor Points, (-5%) Hit % For Duration Of Combat
[*] [b]Shanker’s Hours: [/b](-2) Damage For All Melee Attacks Against
[*] [b]Gunning For You:[/b] (-2) Damage For All Ranged Attacks Against
[*] [b]Hit Me Again: [/b](+2) Armor Points if Temporarily Injured
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]Strong Back: [/b](+20) Hitpoints, (-5%) Critical % For Duration Of Combat
[*] [b]Stubborn Bastard:[/b] (20%) Chance Of Gaining (+5) Hitpoints After Each Round
[*] [b]Too Stupid To Fall:[/b] No Critical Damage Against
[*] [b]Pack Animal:[/b] Negates Stamina Penalties From Helmets, Armor, And Shields
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/8e859c74e910587c2030a218e9d17ac63f89815e.png[/img]

[h1][b]Brutician[/b][/h1]
[i]“Some consider me a healer -- others an inspirer. Whatever I am, you can't lose with me in your group.”[/i]
[list]
[*] [b]How's The Breath?: [/b]Restores (1) Stamina Of Team Members
[*] [b]Dog Of War: [/b](+2) Stamina
[*] [b]Can’t Touch This:[/b] (5%) Block Chance
[*] [b]The Departed: [/b](+1) Damage To Team For Every Dead Team Member  (Does Not Stack)
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]Pass Me The Tape:[/b] Restores (5) Hitpoints Of Team Members
[*] [b]Rock N Roll:[/b] (+2) Stamina To Any Team Member Afflicted With A Disease (Does Not Stack)
[*] [b]Cornered Tiger:[/b] (+2) Stamina To Any Team Member Afflicted With An Injury (Does Not Stack)
[*] [b]What's Wrong?:[/b] (-1) Damage All Opposing Units (Stacks With Up To 5 Other Bruticians)
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]Roll The Dice:[/b] (+30%) Critical % For Both Friendly And Enemy Fighters (Does Not Stack)
[*] [b]No Gumption:[/b] (-1) Hit % All Opposing Units (Stacks With Up To 5 Other Bruticians)
[*] [b]Old Sport:[/b] If Hitpoints (5) Or Below, (+3) Damage To Team For Combat Duration (Does Not Stack)
[*] [b]Shit Disturber:[/b] (+2) Damage To Every Team Member (Stacks With Up To 5 Other Bruticians)
[/list]	
[list]
[*] [b]Pass Me The Mop:[/b] Restores (10) Hitpoints Of Team Members
[*] [b]He Was An Asshole:[/b] (+3) Hit % To Team If Dead
[*] [b]Doctor Death:[/b] (+2) Damage With Each Team Heal Or Stamina Recovery Action Used
[*] [b]Grandpa Snuff:[/b] (+15) Hit % For Any Team Member Over 25 Years Of Age
[/list]

As you saw in my earlier post about weapons here, each weapon type (1h Edged, 2h Edged, 1h Blunt, 2h Blunt, 1h Ranged, and 2h Ranged) has a unique set of attacks. Combined with class Perks, there’s a lot of room for customizing and tactical experimentation.

Some of the above may change as launch day comes closer, but this should give you an idea for now of the various abilities available to raiders. 

More to come!

notes.title: Devlog #13 - Weapon Modifications
notes.content:
Weapons are important part of life in the wasteland. Whether a weapon is looted or crafted, a good pistol or a sturdy baseball bat is an important aspect of survival.

See [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/972010/announcements/detail/1582374841959698529][b]Devblog #4[/b][/url] for more info on weapons. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/7b723510c105df80015a88e189c199a4ba071b21.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/9820a0a86138869103131f92ed7087e145b9c5f4.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/cc6a59928b66a836c3268ab0bf75f4e111778086.png[/img]

[h1]Modifications[/h1]

Weapons can be further modified by components looted from battle. For example, a baseball bat can be made more accurate with handle-grips or more deadly with surface shards. Another example would be a scope on a rifle for increased accuracy or a extended magazines for more ammo capacity. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/119126c5e4b32ede5d1789d790cd252ce23f9a0e.png[/img] 

Each weapon class has its own set of applicable modifications:
[list]
[*] Edged 1-Handed
[*] Edged 2-Handed
[*] Blunt 1-Handed
[*] Blunt 2-Handed
[*] Ranged 1-Handed
[*] Ranged 2-Handed
[/list]
Weapons are modified from the crafting screen and each one can have up to three modifications attached to it. 

So not only do weapons have variable stats, but these stats can further be improved through looted components. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/644e8ee192d4c6d4c442d980000402c3b311286e.png[/img]

More to come!

notes.title: Devlog #12 - Buildings & Labour
notes.content:
Maintaining your hideout is one of the most important aspects of the game. Providing your raiders with a well-stocked hideout in terms of food, water, and beer is crucial - but equally so are the construction of buildings to keep your organization running smoothly. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/c5db15eae15a7cc5e8860ad253bf0910288ccf85.png[/img]

There's an assortment of buildings that can be constructed if you have enough wood and scrap. Buildings can serve many purposes, some converting raw ingredients into consumables, such as a Brewery (barley into beer), Ammo Press (saltpeter into ammo), a Butcher (cows into meat) and many more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/8c9dc0ba00372190b8315da88e3b7341a74eef2b.png[/img]

Other buildings serve other purposes for your organization, such as the Gambling Den (increasing morale), the Counterfeit Shop (manufacturing fake currency), Salt Shacks (decreasing chances of sickness), a Water Well (generating water), the Fight Pits (passively increasing XP) and more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/44c13d37feea126b355c03756a66c93e1f462527.png[/img]

There are many other building types as well.

In order to construct certain buildings, you will require the services of a specialist in your organization. These people are typically captured in the wasteland and pressed into service. Some examples of specialists include a Madame (for the brothel), an Armorsmith (for the armor shop), a Surgeon (for building the hospital), a smelter (for building the furnace), and more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/db3530cc99ca586f0669778ed98da73207231705.png[/img]

[h1]Labor[/h1]

Once a building is constructed, it must be populated with Workers (in addition to the Specialist which oversees the operation of the building itself. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/fdb8a94663874a3cd50b267a2ad1e272ebc0b380.png[/img]

Workers can be extorted from settlements, captured after battle, or purchased from slavers. Once workers have been acquired, they must then be brought back to your hideout. They can then either be assigned to a building, or if your raiders are hungry, can be butchered for meat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/33db5c5e14e4380b81b90809e7714e2daa6e8c88.png[/img]

Each building can have up to five workers assigned, improving the output of that particular building. So it's important to pick and choose which buildings you want to be outputting at maximum efficiency, as workers in the wasteland are hard to come by (at least without a fight).

Hope you enjoyed this -- I'll continue to keep you posted on the game's mechanics.

notes.title: Devlog #11 - Sieges & Fortifications
notes.content:
As you go around knocking off settlements, caravans, and various industries of the wasteland, your infamy will continue to grow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/4f540088665ef92e3343e5dd5094a59abc79955f.png[/img]

When this happens, sedentary locations will start to set aside a bit of manpower to build fortifications to defend against your attack: ditches, mounds, pikes, walls, gates, and bunkers. Attacking a fortification without first taking them down will inflict brutal wounds on your raiders.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/ef69fb6c12e9d5bce69b2ba4a96052e2221dba27.png[/img]

Rejoice though, siege weapons can be built which have a chance of taking down a number of fortifications. This is determined by a simple dice roll where the number of fortifications that fall is dependent on the dice roll and the attack rating of the weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/dcc141f56d7525f430bde9c15fc3226abf39ce81.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/246a00c11d3ee0c60f67fdad20fb7a5de2aedda7.png[/img]

It's important to know that your siege machine will eventually be destroyed during combat, so build and use them wisely.

[h1]Your Own Fortifications[/h1]

The good news is that you can also build your own fortifications in both your hideout as well as any locations that you manage to capture.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/5ff81121fdcf3d66edc6e5e2a69e725ad0570308.png[/img]

That means enemy regulators and mercenaries will injure themselves on your pikes and walls as well.

notes.title: Devlog #10 - Hostages, Specialists, and Laborers!
notes.content:
Caravans in the wasteland aren’t always just carrying resources – sometimes their cargo is human. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/20e769a9b2a8b0b6407d338ef9a7727e7115f252.png[/img]

[h1]Specialists[/h1]

Some of those people may be valuable to your organization, folks like carpenters, engineers, armorsmiths, chemists, coopers, scribes, jesters, scavengers, smelters, brewers, and more.
Specialists provide bonuses, unlock buildings for construction in your hideout, and more. 
Once you capture one of these individuals, they will be pressed into service, applying their trade in earnest. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/34c01aa26f7a5f651c07a4e32b398f72fdedf4ba.png[/img]

[h1]Hostages[/h1]

Some caravans will be carrying VIPs instead.

Knocking off one of these caravans will yield a VIP – however, unlike specialists and tradesmen, these so-called “important” people to the settlements of the wasteland are useless to your own organization, so you can take them hostage instead.

The settlements will pay dearly for their release, depending on their importance.
Your options are to either ransom them (for chips), execute them (for fear), or butcher them (for meat). If you’re of the kinder disposition, you can also free them without ransom for a drop in infamy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/8032d0bfc67555bf90b8edbd15ffc9793c67a788.png[/img]

[h1]Laborers[/h1]

General laborers are also valuable. No settlement will pay for their release and they aren’t as important as specialized tradesmen, but they still serve a purpose. You can obtain workers from raids, from demands, and from slavers.

The more workers you have in your hideout, the faster things are built. Workers can also be assigned to buildings to increase their efficiency. 

So go forth an plunder – resources and money aren’t the only thing you can steal!

notes.title: Devlog #9 - Resources, Scavenging, and Crafting
notes.content:
[h1]Resources[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/4489b988b681eb53ac3b7070305a5138f52db1fc.png[/img]

There are many ways of obtaining the resources required to run a successful operation:
[list]
[*] Scavenging
[*] Looting
[*] Extorting
[*] Purchasing
[/list]
Occasionally you can capture a specialist such as a wood scavenger or water diviner who will find resources for you each day. 

Resources are used to build things in your base, such as alcohol stills, gambling dens, fortifications and other assorted structures.

The other use for resources is crafting, which will be the focus of this devlog.

[h1]Scavenging[/h1]

Roaming the wasteland, you will discover the leavings of past civilizations. Scattered metal, wood, and garbage will give you enough to get started.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/49c2ff9f195463aa8db71c865ee1032cc717d090.png[/img]

[h1]Crafting[/h1]

Weapons, Armor, Shields, Helmets and Siege Machines can all be crafted in the game. While crafting isn’t completely necessary, the equipment you craft can come out better than looted or purchased equivalents, depending on the success of the crafting session.
In order to craft an item, you will require one of or a combination of wood, plastic, metal, cloth, and leather.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/be3ed73a196ce96406aa4aed7ed73ecb1a8a0a08.png[/img]

[h1]Reverse Engineering[/h1]
To craft an item, you must possess the recipe for that item. And to obtain a recipe, you must break-down the item you wish to craft. So ultimately, you will have to loot and purchase items in order to break them down. 

But once you have broken down an item, you will have that recipe for the entirety of that playthrough.

Breaking down an item will also return a portion of the resources used to build it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/437c9f6273956e6a9de3dba9a048654fc8b3071b.png[/img] 

[h1]Summary[/h1]

Until a raider organization can become self-sufficient with crews of scavengers scouring the wastelands, you will have to do it yourself. Luckily the detritus of the past civilizations will be enough to get you started – but in order to truly strive, you will need to fight and extort the denizens of the wasteland in order to get what you need.

You are raiders after all.

notes.title: Devlog #8 - Weapons Of Mass Destruction
notes.content:
Imagine the pure joy a raider feels when wiping the dust away from a metal container and spotting for the first time a nuclear hazard symbol on the side. 

The mind races with possibilities, considering who or what to target first. Perhaps the stubborn air craft carrier base holding three raiders prisoner or that coveted settlement with the massive garrison... 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/bb7474b31d2c274c92070d170d0880528b48b78d.png[/img]

[h1]Scavenging[/h1]

Though the wasteland is harsh and unforgiving, there is much scavenge from the ancients that can be recovered. Most of it is scrap (for turning into crafting steel), wood (for building up and fortifying your hideout), or garbage (for turning into plastics) -- but occasionally, one might come across the husk of an old world bomber or submarine.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/19adbba48de7f874fe68aa2d6340ec094c2b74e1.png[/img]

Poking around inside might yield a rare surprise: a canister of napalm perhaps. Or a tactical nuke. Maybe some mustard gas. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/fb30ba44e01cc38245c7ec31a7c416064b648062.png[/img]

[h1]Committing Atrocities[/h1]

As your infamy rises in the wasteland, the local settlements will increase their garrisons and fortifications. When this happens, it might become too costly to attack without deploying siege devices or weapons of mass destruction first.

You could smash your forces against an impenetrable defense, but this would be suicidal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/32d16d21f17ecfc90a757a32bd96263c506da3a9.png[/img]

If you have a tactical nuke or other weapon of mass destruction handy in your back-pocket, why not deploy that instead? You know you want to.

Committing an atrocity will clear a percentage of the garrison, depending on your success. With fewer enemies to fight, you should be able to successfully attack the settlement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/ccc68c9367febdf5340d68e602463dc553468efb.png[/img]

[h1]Use Your WMD Responsibly[/h1]

Of course, this will have the adverse effect of raising your infamy in the area and causing other settlements and surrounding industry to further increase their garrisons and fortifications -- so be mindful of when and where you deploy one of these terrible (useful) weapons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35600581/3370d993b7967de7b3cc07d8628eb8aa3ae8ec47.png[/img]

notes.title: Devlog #7 - The Wheel Of Laws
notes.content:
Even the wildest of wasteland raiders require some semblance of order in their lives. No one knows how the ancient tradition started, but the wheel of laws has been a staple in your raider organization for many years now.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/af741f9d80b71b574830973ac5e94dce429da240.png[/img] 

[h1]The Wheel Has Spoken[/h1]
As leader of your organization, you can occasionally opt to spin the wheel of laws, adopting or declining whatever law it lands on. 

Each spin of the wheel costs 500 "Fear" (a currency of the wasteland used for many things, including extortion and avoiding combat with regulators sent after you). A spin of the wheel might land on a law that you don't want, so there's a definite risk as each law carries one bonus and one penalty. Both are permanent. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/cdf34ec461b4a51acd6ed62da41853b57e90668f.png[/img]

[h1]Laws Of The Wasteland[/h1] 
Examples of laws include alcohol prohibition, headhunting, rules of profit, cannibalism, settlement occupation, succession rites, and various other cultural and tactical rules of engagement. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/3b0523f1657bff3a9af9ca61d7719a3a90ff54d8.png[/img] 

As laws in your organization accumulate over time, they will govern how you and your raiders comport themselves in the wasteland...

notes.title: Devlog #6 - Treasure & Currency
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/d21ecf253a6fb4c3ce7845d12055800633c509de.png[/img]

Caravans in the wasteland will usually be carrying produce or supplies such as scavenged plastic, scrap metal, wood, barley, cattle, and more. All of these are vital to a raider operation -- but occasionally, you may receive intelligence of a treasure convoy carrying an ancient artifact from one settlement to the next.

Sure, televisions sets and old cars are also considered ancient artifacts... but these are truly ancient. Old items plundered (or saved) from the world's museums before the great catastrophes, items such as the Euphonious Krater, the Canopic Jars, and the Pharaoh Death Mask for example... items that will provide valuable insight into the past cultures and civilizations of our planet if reconstruction and recovery ever takes place.

Naturally though, you're of the mind that these priceless artifacts would look better in your own collection...

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/a8e4d5cf1c9b0a762e98636c6b6e927f56ab62c8.jpg[/img]
Treasures not only tie your treasure room together, but also provide organizational bonuses as well. Incredibly rare in the wasteland, it's a big deal if you are able loot an artifact of importance.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/0c0bac672352524455782b5a41f9805e40322c70.png[/img]

[h1]Casino Chips[/h1]
The main tendered currency of the wasteland was deemed to be casino chips.

People considered other items, bottle caps for instance - but casino chips were deemed more practical in the long run. Small, colorful, plastic objects with numbers on them... it sort of made sense. So now, people fight and die over them.

Of course, there are many ways of obtaining chips in the wasteland if you're an unsavory fellow: for example, you can attack people for them, you can trade produce for them (stolen, looted, or generated from captured industry), you can exchange captured hostages for them, or you can counterfeit them (if you have built a plastic mold in your hideout).

Your raiders depend on a steady supply of chips streaming in - feed their greed or watch their morale start to drop...

notes.title: Devlog #5 - Helmets, Armor, and Special Items
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/04fb1a944decfa5ee962a3b1af65b744ca768728.png[/img]

Like weapons, combatants in the wasteland equip themselves with whatever mishmash of helmets, armor, or shields that they are able to scavenge, loot, or craft (will discuss crafting, components and reverse-engineering in a separate Devlog). 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/5c3a5c7c30f8437fd947f72e396b9b9463730345.png[/img]

[h1]Helmets[/h1]

Helmets offer a variety of protections, but also stamina and hit chance penalties. 

For example, light helmets offer little to no protection, but they look kind of cool, so you might want to equip your raiders with these. Light helmets include caps, sun visors, and potato sacks. Oh, and the wearer suffers from no penalties.

On the flip side, very heavy helmets (think of cumbersome Deep Sea helmets, Riot helmets, and more), offer massive protections, but also massive stamina and hit chance penalties, as the wearer won't be able to see for more than 30 degrees in either direction. 

Helmets come in the following categories:

[list]
[*]Light[- little to no protection, no stamina and hit % penalties.
[*]Medium- middling protection, small stamina and hit % penalties
[*]Heavy- heavy protection, but also heavy stamina and hit % penalties.
[*]Very Heavy - extremely heavy protection, extremely heavy stamina and hit % penalties.
[/list]

Examples of helmets include:

[list]
[*]Riot Helmet
[*]Deep Sea Helmet
[*]Skull Helmet
[*]Combat Helmet
[*]Horned Helmet
[*]GI Helmet
[*]Football Helmet
[*]Hockey Helmet
[*]Ned Kelly Helmet
[*]Welding Helmet
[*]Plumed Raider Mask

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/d5fe1d6b59449b59c508da410c222a5190aaac8f.png[/img]

[h1]Armor[/h1]

Similar to helmets, armor also offers varying degrees of protection and penalties.

Armor comes in the following categories:

[list]
[*]Light - little to no protection, no stamina and hit % penalties.
[*]Medium - middling protection, small stamina and hit % penalties
[*]Heavy - heavy protection, but also heavy stamina and hit % penalties.
[*]Very Heavy - extremely heavy protection, extremely heavy stamina and hit % penalties.
[/list]

Examples of the armor sets include:

[list]

So you have the choice of rolling out a deadly but fragile glass-cannon or a lumbering beast that takes no damage, but can't dodge or attack very well. 

The choice is yours.

[h1]Shields[/h1]

I don't currently have any artwork done for shields, but will have something to show soon enough.

Raiders can also equip themselves with shields, offering protection in addition to their armor and helmet. However, equipping a shield precludes the equipping as well of any two-handed weapons. So again, the choice becomes whether you want to roll out a damage dealer or a damage soaker.

Examples of shields include:

Shields offer varying degrees of protection - for example, a riot shield will be much more efficacious in battle than a highway sign... but a raider will sometimes make due with whatever they have.

notes.title: Devlog #3 - Meat, Beer, Hippos and Cannibalism
notes.content:
[h1][b]Meat and Water[/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/9b9b8d87e416c07ef29a795b11cfb3b67c7208f5.png[/img]

Survivors in the wasteland sustain themselves on small diets of meat and water extracted from the unforgiving land. Meat and water are self-explanatory – without either, people start dropping like flies. So when planning a trip of marauding and destruction out in the wasteland, make sure your raiders are adequately supplied first. 
 
Of course, there are farms and settlements that you can raid for food. You could also build a well in your hideout. Or if you’re fortunate, you can find the odd oasis which will supply you with fresh water – just watch out for any ornery hippos bathing there as they can kill a man with one bite.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/ccf1944e3db7fe3edf6461e236ff18f62a7c8e69.png[/img]

[h1][b]Beer[/b][/h1]

Barley is also grown in select farms, but this is never consumed directly – no, these sacred grains are used to brew beer instead.  

Raiders like beer. They’re day-drinking piss-tanks in fact. With a daily ration of beer, their morale remains stable – and being drunk, they’ll fight more fearlessly in battles. So keeping your raiders supplied with booze is important.

Short-term solutions include raiding or extorting caravans and settlements in the area for their beer. 

However, a more long-term solution would be to capture a barley farm, kidnap a brewer, and construct a still in your hideout. Congratulations, you have embraced vertical integration and are now a beer manufacturer. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/cd872a2cfcd781bf62cbaf70c5868d276cc3f033.png[/img]
 
[h1][b]Cannibalism[/b][/h1]

There are times you will run out of food.

During those times, you might opt to butcher some of your camels or cows for meat. But if you don’t have any captured livestock, humans might be the next viable item on the menu. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/8da8d9dfa8111c1c4816119651e3bbc348ac2c99.png[/img]

Perhaps you’ve captured some workers from the nearby quarry or farm and are leading them back to your hideout to put them to work – but your raiders are starving. No one will notice if you butcher one or two prisoners, right?

Or if you have higher value hostages, perhaps you can throw them in the pot.
The last resort would be butchering one of your own raiders. 

Pity the poor sap that draws the short-straw…

notes.title: Devlog #2 - Leadership, Succession, Promotions, And Duels (Pre-Alpha)
notes.content:
[h1][b]Leadership[/b][/h1]

In Raiders, you play as the leader of a band of marauders. 

But instead of running your organization from afar, your character must eat, drink, deal with potential insurrections, and engage in combat. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/d9cf7894ecc4c442478446580ff5d0d38cd0187a.png[/img]

[h1][b]Succession Or Permadeath[/b][/h1]

Because your character exists within the world, dying is a possibility. Depending on your game settings, this will either result in your game ending, or one of your raiders taking up the mantle of command instead. 

They will become your new character, meaning you can play for as long as you wish if you have at least one raider still surviving. 

[h1][b]Leadership Points[/b][/h1]

Because the player is a unit like the rest of the raiders under your command, your character will gain experience points from activities in the wasteland and level up. However, your character will also have a second set of exclusive attributes to level up as well that will provide direct benefits to the leading of your organization.

These attributes include the following:

[b]Negotiation:[/b] Lowers the costs of bribing away enemy parties sent to attack you. 
[b]Intimidation:[/b] Increases the amount of fear you gain from raider activities. Fear is used to extort resources from enemy settlements and caravans.
[b]Determination:[/b] Increases the weight capacity of your raider party.
[b]Organization:[/b] Reduces the construction time of hideout buildings and fortifications.
[b]Logistics:[/b] Increases the unit capacity of your party and garrisons. 
[b]Subterfuge:[/b] Reduces the amount of infamy gained from raider activities. Infamy determines the fortification level of settlements, as well as the strength of caravan guards and mercenary parties sent to kill you. 
[b]Mobilization:[/b] Increases the movement speed of your party.
[b]Cruelty:[/b] Decreases the movement penalty of your party from captives.
[b]Charisma:[/b] Increases the morale gained by the activities of raiders in your party. 
[b]Intuitiveness:[/b] Increases the amount of experience both you and your raiders gain from combat and other activities.
[b]Greed:[/b] Increases the amount of loot and chips (currency) gained from combat.  

[h1][b]Promotions[/b][/h1]

You have the choice of promoting two of your followers to the ranks of Lieutenant and Sergeant respectively. Promoting a follower will provide them with combat and discipline bonuses – however, the downside to promoting a raider is that it might empower them to challenge you for the mantle of leadership…

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/3dfbe289592bc8159b67c7a57367065b7f6a9439.png[/img]

[h1][b]Leadership Duels[/b][/h1]

Occasionally, if morale drops within your organization, you will be challenged to a duel. This can only happen however if you promote a raider to either Lieutenant or Sergeant. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/5ab56fc7afad2d7037230a9fd12b22bef8c1fa56.png[/img]

If your character is challenged to a duel, it will be a one-on-one fight to the death with the challenger. If your character perishes, your game will either end or leadership will be passed to the new victor where you will continue playing.


[h1][b]Burden of Command[/b][/h1]

I hope this provides some insight into the extra layer of gameplay I instituted into Raiders. You are not a god-like leader, looking down on your organization from afar...instead you are a character living in the world that must fight, eat, deal with insurrections, plan for successions, and more! 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/e76daeaf6315087777c15cb8b98f89e205642703.png[/img]

notes.title: Devlog #1 - The World (Pre-Alpha)
notes.content:
[h1]The World[/h1]

The world of Raiders takes place on the receding, desertified ocean floor. Husks of crashed bombers, ships, cargo containers, whale skeletons, and more litter the salt-stained dunes.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/ef050d071e0efa07883f1af80c9d6d5329328635.png[/img]

[h1][b]Settlements[/b][/h1]

From these sweltering dunes, settlements have appeared, assembled from whatever their denizens are to scavenge. Eking out an hard-scrabbled existence any way they can in the wasteland, the denizens of the settlements have become hardy survivors over the years.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/bbc2b075be958865c73194323ca257158ddaf9b9.png[/img]

[h1]Industry[/h1]

Industries such as garbage scavengers, scrap smelters, camel ranches, and more have also emerged in order to provide resources and materials for these settlements.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/635424d428951aa3d2bb8be3252492764d528cd0.png[/img]

[h1]Caravans[/h1]

These resources are transported to the settlements via the use of caravans, hundreds dotting the landscape, carrying their precious cargoes of resources, scavenged old-world treasures, and travelers.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/97969a4140777b3198fb0e9e714c7e034724c594.png[/img]

[h1]Raiders[/h1]

So what's the by-product of all these settlements, industries, caravans, and tribes? Raiders. Your people -- a people possessing a long and proud tradition of sticking their middle-finger up at the notion of a hard-day's work and choosing the marauder's way instead. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/35600581/7a249f2c6e59fca160dba8fda3b9695d465c743e.png[/img]

Of course, a raider party will have to consider who they attack. Caravans pose the easiest targets, but as a raider organization grows, industries, settlements, and citadels will eventually pose more tempting targets...

The world is a chaotic place.

[h1]And the wasteland doesn't need another hero.[/h1]
